title: Unit test 'device ACL requires device or nonzero master token' fails on master
description:
indigo_test/unit/test_protocol_security.c device_acl_requires_device_or_nonzero_master_token fails deterministically on master ddd7ad5b6 without any task change, so make -C indigo_test test-unit stops there and does not run the suites after it. Either the device/master token ACL in the XML/JSON request parsers or the test expectation regressed; not investigated in the origin task, which does not touch the protocol code. Next: find which of the four assertions fails, bisect since d02bc87dc, fix and rerun the unit suite.

Imported from .factory/findings/active/FND-20261112204155-dae8-warn-sync-near-pole-001.json (category: quality, blocking: no).

outcome.summary: Net diff vs master touches only indigo_test/unit/test_protocol_security.c (git diff master -- indigo_libs empty). The changed expectation (device token set, master token 0, tokenless request delivered) matches INDIGO_DEVICE_ACCESS_CONTROL_AND_LOCKING.md (Protected Devices; Master Tokens: without a master token no devices can be protected) and indigo_change_property() at indigo_bus.c:1013, whose semantics date from d834de662/94c2caee2 (2020) and were never changed; the old expectation came from b53c9d145 (unrelated Sequencer commit) and was never implemented. Owner chose the documented contract (question/answer in journal). Assertion is non-vacuous (changes == 1); rejected_with_master still fails if the ACL were removed, accepted_without_master fails if tokenless requests were refused regardless of master, device/master-token acceptance asserts unchanged; both XML and JSON paths covered. Formatting: tabs, one-line calls, no blank lines; git diff --check clean. Reviewer reran make -C indigo_test test-unit in the worktree: exit 0, 39/39 UNIT_TESTS suites ran (78 Running lines), 512 PASS, 0 FAIL, binary rebuilt after the source edit. Non-blocking: the test name now reads ambiguously; out of scope: with master 0 a request carrying a wrong nonzero token is still refused, which the doc's 'no effect' wording does not describe.

Reproduction (worktree source, before fix): build/unit/test_protocol_security prints 'FAIL device ACL requires device or nonzero master token'. Cause: indigo_bus.c indigo_change_property() accepted a request when property->access_token == indigo_get_master_token(); with no master token set (0) a tokenless request (0) matched and bypassed a device token. Test added in b53c9d145 with the intended contract (nonzero master token only); the check dates from 94c2caee2 (2020), so it is a long-standing hole, not a recent regression, and the test expectation is right.

After fix (master token must be nonzero to match): worktree make -C indigo_test test-unit exits 0, 0 FAIL, 512 PASS lines, test_protocol_security all pass. Worktree build: make Makefile.inc; make init; make -C indigo_libs all (~3 min incl. externals); 104 driver archives via make -C indigo_drivers/D all (30s, -P8); suite 101s.

Check command-1 failed: exit code 2

Check command-1 passed

The failing assertion expects a tokenless request to be refused by a device with a device token when the server has no master token. indigo_docs/INDIGO_DEVICE_ACCESS_CONTROL_AND_LOCKING.md states the opposite contract ('the server must have master token set, otherwise device tokens will have no effect'; 'if the server has no master token set ... no devices can be protected, even if they have device token set'), and indigo_bus.c has implemented that since 94c2caee2 (2020). The test was added in b53c9d145 (2026-11-05). The implementer changed indigo_bus.c to satisfy the test, which changes documented protocol behaviour. Which is the intended contract: (a) the documented one - revert the indigo_bus.c change and correct the test expectation for the no-master case; (b) the stricter one - keep the indigo_bus.c change and update the documentation?

Owner (2026-11-15): option (a). The documented contract holds: without a server master token device tokens have no effect. Revert the indigo_bus.c change and correct the test expectation for the no-master case.
Reverting bus fix on owner decision; correcting test expectation

The first fix (indigo_bus.c master-token check) was REVERTED on the owner's decision: INDIGO_DEVICE_ACCESS_CONTROL_AND_LOCKING.md states that without a master token device tokens have no effect, and indigo_bus.c has implemented that since 94c2caee2. Test corrected instead: with device token set and master 0 a tokenless request is delivered (changes == 1); other three assertions unchanged. indigo_libs identical to master.
